table_title: List the longest-main-span bridges of the world's major structural types — top 4 of each of the four primary load-bearing types (suspension, cable-stayed, arch, cantilever) plus the longest continuous truss bridge — with each bridge's structural type, main span length in metres, country, and year of completion. Source universe is Wikipedia's per-type 'List of longest X bridge spans' master articles.
db_analog: SELECT b.bridge_name AS bridge, b.structural_type AS type, b.main_span_m AS main_span, b.country, b.year_of_completion AS year FROM bridges b WHERE (b.structural_type IN ('Suspension','Cable-stayed','Arch','Cantilever') AND b.type_rank <= 4) OR (b.structural_type = 'Continuous truss' AND b.type_rank = 1) ORDER BY b.structural_type ASC, b.main_span_m DESC
temporal_note: Wikipedia per-type 'List of longest X bridge spans' master articles + 17 per-bridge Wikipedia articles, all accessed 2026-05-13. Universe = top-4 longest-main-span bridges per each of the four primary load-bearing structural types (Suspension, Cable-stayed, Arch, Cantilever), plus the single longest continuous truss bridge (Ikitsuki Bridge, Japan). Total 17 rows across 5 structural types. The 4+1 partition asymmetry is a curator-decision documented in curation.json::decision_log: the continuous truss type is included as a type-#1-only entry because the top-4 floor of continuous truss bridges (~325m) falls well below the visible engineering threshold the other four primary types occupy (all 4th-place entries exceed 500m), making a type-#1 anchor more informative than a forced top-4 fill. temporal_sensitivity = medium because the master per-type lists update as new long-span bridges complete (especially in China, where multiple historical 4th-place entries have been displaced over the past 5 years — cycle-2 audit caught two such recent displacements: Xihoumen Bridge displaced from Suspension top-4 by Nanjing Xianxin Yangtze River Bridge (1760 m, 2025); Stonecutters Bridge displaced from Cable-stayed top-4 by Husutong Yangtze River Bridge (1092 m, 2020)). Within the staged 17 rows, three Suspension/Cable-stayed entries are 2020-2025 completions (1915 Çanakkale 2022, Changtai Yangtze 2025, Nanjing Xianxin 2025) and these rankings may shift again within 5-10 years as additional Yangtze-crossing mega-bridges are completed. Per-row Year of Completion follows the per-bridge Wikipedia article's lead/infobox 'completed' or 'opened' year (calendar year of opening to traffic for road bridges, calendar year of completion for cantilever bridges where opening is staged).
_extraction_notes: Top_k instance with hierarchical_decomposition secondary: per-type partitioned top-K, where the universe is partitioned by structural type (5 types) and within each partition the top-N-by-main-span bridges are included. Partition rule = top-4 for each of the four primary load-bearing types (Suspension, Cable-stayed, Arch, Cantilever) PLUS the top-1 for the Continuous truss type — total 17 rows. Source universe = Wikipedia's five per-type 'List of longest X bridge spans' master articles (one per structural type), each of which is a maintained ranked list by main-span length. Per-row attribute grounding from 17 per-bridge Wikipedia articles (lead/infobox supplies Main Span, Country, Year of Completion). Schema: 5 cols (Bridge PK + Type categorical + Main Span numeric + Country categorical + Year of Completion numeric). Sort: Type ASC primary (alphabetical: Arch, Cable-stayed, Cantilever, Continuous truss, Suspension), Main Span DESC secondary (longest-first within each partition). Distribution by type: Arch 4, Cable-stayed 4, Cantilever 4, Continuous truss 1, Suspension 4 = 17 rows. Country distribution: China 9 (dominates Arch + Cable-stayed + Suspension top-K lists per master rankings — all 4 Arch entries + 3 of 4 Cable-stayed + 2 of 4 Suspension), Japan 3 (Akashi Kaikyō suspension + Minato cantilever + Ikitsuki continuous truss), United States 1, United Kingdom 1, Canada 1, Russia 1, Turkey 1, Denmark/Sweden 0 (Great Belt East Bridge not staged because it sits at Suspension #5-ish, below the top-4 cutoff). Year of Completion range: 1890 (Forth Bridge cantilever) to 2025 (Changtai cable-stayed + Nanjing Xianxin suspension) — 135 years of major-span bridge engineering. Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal + painters + extinctions + deserts + tennis + music-genres + olympians + spacecraft lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Bridge using Wikipedia common-form names with full disambiguator preserved (e.g., '1915 Çanakkale Bridge' includes the disambiguating prefix because the short form 'Çanakkale Bridge' is ambiguous); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 articles each (per-type master list + per-bridge article); (c) explicit selection rule for the 4+1 asymmetric partition (Continuous truss type-#1-only because top-4 floor falls below visible engineering threshold the other types sit above); (d) source_defined claim type (universe is curator-bounded per the 4+1 rule, not exhaustive top-K-uniform-K); (e) Cassini-Huygens-style canonical name preservation (Akashi Kaikyō uses Japanese ō macron per Wikipedia title; 1915 Çanakkale uses Turkish ç cedilla; Tian'e Longtan uses ASCII apostrophe per Wikipedia URL form). Apply Wikipedia common-form naming rule and source-faithful universe definition per PKDB-Bench design philosophy.
